title: What Sri Lanka’s executioners do when no execution is scheduled
byline: Sri Lanka currently has two members serving as executioners. However, the executioners do not remain on standby solely for capital punishment duties. They are regular employees of the Prisons Department, carrying out other assigned duties and receiving standard government salaries until they are called upon for an execution.

title: Welikada gallows ready if death penalty imposed
byline: The Welikada Prison gallows remain ready for use if the government decides to resume executions, with two executioners currently attached to the prison and on standby, the Daily Mirror learns.

title: Lebanon parliament votes to abolish death penalty
byline: Lebanon’s parliament has voted to abolish the death penalty, a move that would make it the first country in the Middle East to formally end capital punishment.

title: Passing through Boralesgamuwa? Check the traffic plan
byline: Temporary traffic restrictions will be imposed in the Boralesgamuwa Police Division on August 13, 14 and 15 in connection with the Bellanwila Esala Maha Perahera, police said.

title: France bans unsolicited telemarketing calls
byline: France has banned unsolicited telemarketing phone calls, in what a consumer group is hailing as a ’’small revolution’’ for the sales industry.

title: Cristiano Ronaldo marries long-time partner Georgina Rodríguez
byline: Football superstar Cristiano Ronaldo has married his longtime partner - model and influencer Georgina Rodríguez - in a civil ceremony in Portugal.

title: Tangalle stray dog population nearly fully covered through sterilization drive
byline: A free sterilization and vaccination programme has covered almost the entire stray and community dog population in the Tangalle Municipal Council area within three months, the Association of Veterinarians for Humane Management of Animal Population said.

title: BASL urges Government to withdraw 22nd Amendment
byline: The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) has urged the Government to refrain from proceeding with the proposed 22nd Amendment to the Constitution in its present form, warning that the proposed extension of the retirement age of Supreme Court and Court of Appeal judges would directly affect the independence of the Judiciary.

title: Protect our elephants on World Elephant Day
byline: Sri Lanka marks World Elephant Day today with renewed calls to protect elephants, safeguard their welfare and promote peaceful coexistence between elephants and people.

title: Oil, gold prices rise as geopolitical tensions mount before CPI
byline: Oil and gold prices climbed while regional shares edged nervously higher on Wednesday as geopolitical tensions ratcheted up ahead of key U.S. inflation data.

title: Trump signs order to limit childhood vaccines and split MMR shots
byline: US President Donald Trump has signed an order that calls for fewer childhood vaccines and also recommends splitting the mumps, measles and rubella (MMR) shots.

title: Forensic audit looms as former state utility pays millions of dollars in equity returns for emergency power
byline: The legacy of state power monopoly has funneled millions of dollars in equity returns to private power producer Ace Power Embilipitiya (Pvt) Ltd over nearly a decade, exposing severe flaws in Sri Lanka’s long-term generation planning and an expensive reliance on emergency procurements.

title: Hikkaduwa–Maradana train delayed after repeated technical issues
byline: Passengers travelling on the Hikkaduwa–Maradana railway line faced delays today after a train developed technical problems at two stations along the route.

title: Tourist arrivals slip by 8% in early August
byline: Sri Lanka’s tourist arrivals opened August on a weaker note than a year earlier, with 42,810 visitors recorded between August 1 and 6, down 8 percent from the 46,541 arrivals over the same six days last year, according to data from the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA).

title: Govt. signals more expansionary measures from 2027 to drive growth
byline: Sri Lanka could see more expansionary measures from 2027 as the government looks to move beyond economic stabilisation towards stronger growth, with small and medium enterprises (SMEs) expected to play a pivotal role in the next phase of the recovery, Deputy Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Chathuranga Abeysinghe said yesterday.

title: Sri Lanka eyes bigger share of India’s gem and jewellery market
byline: Sri Lanka is stepping up efforts to expand its gem and jewellery footprint in India, seeking stronger buyer links, sourcing partnerships and investment as it targets one of the world’s largest jewellery manufacturing and trading markets.

title: Yoshitha Rajapaksa leaves CID
byline: Former President Mahinda Rajapaksa’s son Yoshitha Rajapaksa left the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) a short while ago after recording a statement.

title: Taliban have barred 2.4 million Afghan girls from school since 2021, UNESCO says
byline: The Taliban have barred an estimated 2.4 ‌million Afghan girls from secondary education since they regained power in Afghanistan in 2021, the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization said on Tuesday.

title: Sugeeshwara Bandara further remanded
byline: The Colombo Fort Magistrate’s Court today ordered former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa’s former Private Secretary, Sugeeshwara Lenin Bandara, to be further remanded till August 25 over allegations of criminal misappropriation of funds allocated under the Presidential Expenditure Head.

title: New attacks on shipping as Iran war talks hit fresh impasse
byline: The U.S. and Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis reported separate attacks on shipping on Tuesday as prospects for ending the Iran war appeared to dim, with Tehran saying the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed unless ​Washington accepts its conditions.

title: Protests with burning torches
byline: Residents of several areas in Mahiyangana including Rideemaliyedda, and Nagadiwa Scheme on Monday night (10) staged a massive protest holding burning torches accusing the government of neglecting the threat of wild elephants.

title: Attempt to save snake ends in three-vehicle crash
byline: Three vehicles were damaged and three people were injured after a driver braked suddenly to avoid a snake crossing the Southern Expressway yesterday (11), police said.

title: No increase in MPs’ basic salaries, Cabinet Spokesman says
byline: Cabinet Spokesman Minister Nalinda Jayatissa yesterday (11) denied claims that the basic salaries of Members of Parliament have been increased, saying there has been no revision to MPs’ basic pay.

title: Yoshitha Rajapaksa arrives at CID
byline: Yoshitha Rajapaksa, the son of former President Mahinda Rajapaksa, arrived at the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) today to provide a statement in connection with an ongoing investigation.

title: Gunmen open fire at Tangalle house
byline: A house belonging to a fisheries boat owner in the Kudawella area of Tangalle was targeted in a shooting early this morning (12), police said.

title: Death penalty for drug offences only a proposal: Govt.
byline: The possible imposition of the death penalty for drug-related offences remains only a proposal, with no final decision having been taken by the Government, Cabinet Spokesman Minister Nalinda Jayatissa said yesterday (11).

title: Court finds favouritism, illegality in Peradeniya lecturer selection
byline: The Court of Appeal ordered the University of Peradeniya to appoint a Senior Lecturer Grade II in Buddhist Studies to the post of Senior Lecturer Grade I, after finding that the selection process had been tainted by illegality, procedural unfairness, favouritism and mala fides.

title: Government trying to disable Judiciary and create dictatorship: Sajith
byline: The Government is out to disable the Judiciary and create a dictatorship, Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa said today.

title: Pramodya to take legal action over premature termination of tenure
byline: Former Sri Lanka Cricket Selection Committee Chairman Pramodya Wickramasinghe has decided to take legal action against Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) and the Cricket Transformation Committee over the premature termination of his tenure.

title: Japan sounds alarm as North Korea launches suspected ballistic missile
byline: The Japanese Prime Minister’s Office on Wednesday issued an emergency alert saying North Korea had launched a suspected ballistic missile. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi immediately instructed relevant officials to make every effort to gather information and provide it to the public in a timely and appropriate manner.

title: Dikwella makes Test return as Sri Lanka name India squad
byline: Sri Lanka Cricket’s Selection Committee has announced a 16-member squad for the first Test of the upcoming two-match series against India. The opening match, part of the ICC World Test Championship 2025–2027 cycle, is scheduled to be played at the Galle International Cricket Stadium from August 15 to 19, 2026.

title: 22nd Amendment: Sujeewa makes Chief Prelates’ letter public
byline: SJB MP Sujeewa Senasinghe on Wednesday (12) made public a letter sent by the Chief Prelates of Sri Lanka’s three Buddhist Chapters to President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, urging the Government not to proceed with the proposed 22nd Amendment to the Constitution to extend the retirement age of superior court judges.

title: President says judges’ retirement age extension not aimed at any individual
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has stressed that the decision to extend the retirement age of judges was not taken with any individual or group in mind, but in the broader public interest.

title: Update: Backhoe Saman’s mother killed in shooting
byline: A woman who was reportedly the mother of underworld figure Backhoe Saman has died after being shot in the Ulhitiya area of Middeniya this afternoon (12).

title: Zhu Rongji, Chinese premier who cajoled economy into modern era, dies at 97
byline: Former Chinese Premier Zhu Rongji, who died on Wednesday aged 97, was never one to mince his words.

title: BASL urges President to consult experts before extending judges’ retirement age
byline: The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) has urged President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to make a decision on the proposed constitutional amendment to extend the retirement age of judges only after conducting a broad consultation with experts, BASL President Rajeev Amarasuriya said.

title: Iran refutes Trump’s claim to ‘control’ Hormuz
byline: Iran has refuted President Donald Trump’s claim that Washington has “total control” of the Strait of Hormuz, saying the critical waterway will remain closed until the United States accepts its demands and changes its “behaviour”.

title: Mahanayake Thera says President has not responded to letter on judges’ retirement age
byline: Malwatta Chapter Mahanayake Thera Most Venerable Thibbatuwawe Sri Sumangala Thera said President Anura Kumara Dissanayake had yet to respond to a letter sent by the Mahanayake Theras concerning the proposed extension of the retirement age of judges.

title: Messi unsure he will play ’much longer’ after father’s death
byline: Messi’s father Jorge was 68 when he died last week following a long illness.

title: Police warn against fake news following viral Kohuwala image
byline: The Sri Lanka Police have warned the public against spreading fake news and unverified information on social media following the circulation of a viral image purportedly showing a dead man on a motorcycle beneath the Kohuwala Bridge.
